item.title: Catholics Around The World Mark Ash Wednesday
item.description: Today is Ash Wednesday. Catholics around the world are marking the beginning of Lent. Many will go to church to have a priest smear ashes on their forehead. The ashes symbolize mourning and penance. They also remind Catholics of their mortality. Many Christians give up something tangible for Lent such as liquor or a favorite food. item.title: Dems Rally Resources
item.description: Texas Democrats are “all in” for this midterm in hopes of winning a state-wide race for the first time in three-decades. Party Chairman Kendall Scudder says they are fielding a candidate for every state and federal office for the first time since 1974. They are planning to spend at least 30-million dollars on resources for candidates across the state, as soon as the primary is over.

item.title: ICE Eyes Offices
item.description: ICE’s planned expansion is heavily concentrated in Texas, with at least nine leasing projects underway. A building on San Antonio’s northwest side is reportedly being eyed for administrative offices. This is separate from a proposed immigrant processing center on the east side. ICE is also looking at offices in suburban Houston, El Paso and Eagle Pass.

item.title: Smuggler Sentencing Delayed
item.description: A big rig driver involved in the nation’s deadliest human smuggling case will have to wait a little longer to learn his fate. Homero Zamorano was set to be sentenced Wednesday in San Antonio federal court but a key witness could not make it. The judge put the trial on hold, but did not say for how long. Zamorano drove a tractor trailer, packed with people, from the Texas border town of Laredo to San Antonio. There was no air conditioning. Forty-seven adults and six children died from the heat.

item.title: Unruly Passenger Forces Emergency Landing
item.description: Passengers experienced a mid-air scare aboard a Delta flight from Houston to Atlanta. A man was reportedly trying to break into the cockpit. The pilot made a u-turn and landed back at Hobby Airport, where they were met by the cops. Houston Police confirmed that a suspect was taken into custody. Delta says in a statement that the customer was exhibiting “unruly and unlawful behavior toward other customers.” It did not mention possible criminal charges.

item.title: Down Payment Report
item.description: A new home-buying report shows that, in Texas, there is a wide swing when it comes to saving up for a down payment. item.title: Family Farms Vanishing
item.description: The number of farmers is shrinking in Texas as kids turn down the chance to take over the family business. Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham called the trend “heartbreaking.” She has launched a plan to get more young people interested in farming. That way Texas farms, she says, won’t have to be sold to international conglomerates.

item.title: Eight Backcountry Skiers Found Dead And 1 Still Missing After California Avalanche
item.description: By BROOKE HESS-HOMEIER, JULIE WATSON and JOHN SEEWER Associated Press NEVADA CITY, Calif.
